objective: Write the player's repertoire as real files: repertoire/london.pgn (White) and repertoire/kid.pgn (Black), one PGN game per line with the line name in a header, plus a pure parser packages/chess-core/src/repertoire-pgn.ts that turns a multi-game PGN text into RepertoireLineInput[] for buildRepertoire. Prove with tests that the files load, every line is legal, and the key-moment detector flags opponent_left_book when the opponent deviates from these lines.
contract:
Requirements: BR-1: the player must be able to handle positions where the opponent has left the London or KID lines they expected. FR-6(a): the app detects with deterministic code when the opponent leaves the player's repertoire line.

User's decision on issue #13 (2026-11-07): use the suggested set, 8-10 moves deep (full moves).
- London (White): 1.d4 2.Bf4 against ...d5, ...Nf6 and ...c5, one main line each.
- King's Indian (Black): Classical, against the London, and against the Fianchetto.

Coordinator's lines (use these; if chess.js rejects one, fix the minimum, keep the idea, and report the change in your return):
repertoire/london.pgn
  [Line "London vs 1...d5"]       1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. e3 e6 4. Nf3 c5 5. c3 Nc6 6. Nbd2 Bd6 7. Bg3 O-O 8. Bd3 b6 9. Ne5
  [Line "London vs 1...Nf6 (g6)"] 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 g6 3. e3 Bg7 4. Nf3 d6 5. h3 O-O 6. Be2 c5 7. c3 Nc6 8. O-O
  [Line "London vs ...c5"]        1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 c5 3. e3 Nc6 4. c3 Nf6 5. Nd2 e6 6. Ngf3 Bd6 7. Bg3 O-O 8. Bd3
repertoire/kid.pgn
  [Line "KID Classical"]          1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. O-O Nc6 8. d5 Ne7 9. Ne1 Nd7
  [Line "KID vs London"]          1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 g6 3. e3 Bg7 4. Nf3 d6 5. h3 O-O 6. Be2 Nbd7 7. O-O Qe8 8. c4 e5 9. Bh2
  [Line "KID Fianchetto"]         1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nf3 Bg7 4. g3 O-O 5. Bg2 d6 6. O-O Nbd7 7. Nc3 e5 8. e4 c6 9. h3 Qb6
Include the standard Seven Tag Roster headers or at least Event and Result ("*") so the files open in normal chess GUIs; [Line] carries the name.

Existing API (packages/chess-core/src/types.ts, repertoire.ts) — do not change it:
  export type Color = "w" | "b";
  export interface RepertoireLineInput { name: string; color: Color; /** Mainline movetext only, e.g. "1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. e3". */ pgn: string; }
  export function buildRepertoire(lines: RepertoireLineInput[]): Repertoire  // parses each with chess.js loadPgn; throws on unparseable or empty; lines sharing a prefix merge
  Repertoire.continuations(history: string[] /* UCI from start */, color): { line: string; moves: {uci, san}[] } | null
  detect(input: DetectorInput): KeyMoment | null  // src/detector.ts; opponent_left_book = { kind, line, expected: string[] (SAN), played: string (SAN) }
  DetectorInput = { playerColor, fenBefore, move (UCI), history (UCI before move), before: Analysis, after: Analysis, repertoire: Repertoire | null, thresholds: { blunderCp, missedWinCp, punishCp } }
Read test/detector.test.ts and test/fixtures.ts for how existing tests build Analysis values for detect().

Parser (src/repertoire-pgn.ts), pure, no fs: parseRepertoirePgn(text: string, color: Color): RepertoireLineInput[]. Splits games, takes the name from [Line "..."] (fall back to [Event "..."]; throw if neither), strips headers, comments {..}, NAGs and the result token, and rejects variations "( ... )" with a clear error (one mainline per game). Throw on a file with no games and on duplicate line names. Tests may read the real files with node:fs (tests may do I/O; src may not).
